text: Hinduism grew up in India over more than three thousand years, and it has no single founder.
Its oldest hymns, the Rigveda, were made more than 3,000 years ago and were learned by heart for centuries.
src: a vast family of traditions that grew up in the Indian subcontinent over more than three thousand years / Hinduism has no founder
c. 1500–1200 BCE: The hymns of the Rigveda, the oldest Hindu scripture / For centuries they were transmitted by memory alone

text: Most Hindus worship one or more gods, such as Vishnu, Shiva and the Goddess, Devi.
Hindus believe in karma: that good and bad actions bring their results, in this life or the next.
src: Most Hindus worship one or more personal gods / The major traditions are devoted to Vishnu / to Shiva / and to the Goddess, Devi
Karma is the law that actions bring their consequences, in this life or the next

text: The Mahabharata is one of the longest poems in the world, with about 100,000 verses.
Inside it, the Bhagavad Gita tells of a talk between the warrior Arjuna and Krishna, whom Hindus see as God.
src: The Mahabharata, at about 100,000 verses one of the longest poems in the world
Within it stands the Bhagavad Gita, a dialogue on the battlefield between the warrior Arjuna and his charioteer Krishna, revealed as God

text: Through trade and the courts of kings, Hindu gods and stories travelled across the sea to Southeast Asia.
In Cambodia, the great temple of Angkor Wat was built for Vishnu more than 800 years ago.
src: Through trade and the courts of Southeast Asia, Hindu gods, epics and ideas of kingship travelled across the Bay of Bengal
Angkor Wat in Cambodia / was built in the early 12th century as a temple to Vishnu

text: Poet-saints, among them a woman named Mirabai, taught that loving devotion to God makes everyone equal.
Some groups were treated as “untouchable” and badly mistreated; India’s laws banned this more than 70 years ago.
src: some of the greatest bhakti poets, such as Mirabai and the Tamil saint Andal, were women / bhakti poets who taught that devotion makes all equal
Below them were communities treated as “untouchable”, subjected to severe discrimination / the constitution of the Republic of India abolished untouchability in 1950

text: Today about 1.2 billion people are Hindus, most of them in India and Nepal.
They worship at home shrines and in great temples, like the Meenakshi temple at Madurai.
src: About 1.2 billion (2020), most of them in India and Nepal
Worship (puja) takes place at home shrines and in temples / the Meenakshi temple at Madurai
